answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost.
